Commentary.Commentary: We are back with the run-chase to begin here at the Hagley Oval! The umpires make their way out to the middle and are followed by New Zealand players who take their respective fielding positions. Steven Smith and Usman Khawaja are the two openers for Australia. Tim Southee, the Kiwi skipper has the new ball and is all in readiness to begin the proceedings. Let's play...
...Fourth Innings...

Right then, Australia require 279 runs to win and complete a whitewash against New Zealand, with plenty of time at their disposal to achieve this target. New Zealand will be disappointed with the manner in which their batting faltered after showing some resilience. Their bowlers will be eager to secure more than a couple of wickets by the end of the third day's play. The Australian openers will be focused on building a strong opening partnership, a facet they have struggled with in this series. The run-chase is about to commence shortly. Stay tuned.

Australia encountered difficulty in claiming wickets after removing Young early in the innings. They endured a lengthy period before Pat Cummins managed to dismiss Williamson, subsequently securing an impressive 4-wicket haul. Nathan Lyon, although introduced relatively late into the bowling attack, made sure the tailenders didn't linger, claiming a crucial 3-wicket haul. They employed a short ball ploy to trouble the Kiwi batters in the second session. However, they didn't get much out of it and also leaked runs dramatically. Josh Hazlewood maintained disciplined lines and lengths, contributing with a solitary wicket by dismissing Daryl Mitchell. The innings witnessed fluctuating fortunes with partnerships flourishing after each wicket. Nevertheless, the Australian bowlers efficiently dismantled the tailenders, limiting the lead to 278 runs by conceding only 23 runs and claiming 4 wickets before the innings concluded.

The Kiwi innings concluded much more rapidly than anticipated following the flurry of wickets towards the backend, with New Zealand's innings wrapping up for a total of 372 runs. However, thanks to aggressive batting by the lower order, they managed to accumulate quick runs. New Zealand suffered an early setback with the dismissal of Will Young, but Tom Latham and Kane Williamson stabilized the innings with an impressive 105-run partnership. Williamson departed after scoring 51, followed by Rachin Ravindra, who contributed a solid 44-run partnership with Tom Latham before Latham was dismissed for a well-compiled 73. Daryl Mitchell maintained the momentum for New Zealand, showing initial caution before accelerating his scoring. Rachin Ravindra also held his ground, crafting a remarkable 82 runs and narrowly missing out on a century by eighteen runs. Following a resilient partnership of 123, New Zealand experienced a swift collapse after Mitchell's departure for 58. However, every batsman who came to the crease ensured quick scoring. Scott Kuggeleijn added a pivotal 44, while Matt Henry's 16 contributed to New Zealand's total of 372 runs on the scoreboard. However, the hosts won't be happy enough as they fell like a pack of cards in the backend.

Tea, Day 3 - SESSION SUMMARY - 25 Overs, 102 runs, and 3 Wickets! The Blackcaps emerged determined to build on their lead, and they executed their plans effectively. Both Rachin Ravindra and Daryl Mitchell looked comfortable at the crease, steadily accumulating runs, with Mitchell reaching a resilient half-century. However, the introduction of the second new ball brought a sudden shift in fortunes as Josh Hazlewood and Pat Cummins struck quickly to dismiss both batters. Tom Blundell's stay at the crease was brief, ended by a spectacular catch from Marnus Labuschagne. Labuschagne's fortunes fluctuated as he went from hero to zero, dropping Scott Kuggeleijn shortly after. This drop proved costly as Scott capitalized on the opportunity, punishing the bowlers and frustrating the Aussie attack with a counterattacking partnership alongside Phillips which currently stands at 49. Despite Australia's short-ball strategy, runs flowed freely, and the Kiwis now hold a significant lead of 251 runs. They aim to extend it beyond the 300-run mark, setting a challenging target for the visitors. Meanwhile, Cummins and his bowlers will be eager to wrap up the Kiwi innings quickly in the final session. Join us at 8.30 am IST (3 am GMT) for what promises to be an exhilarating conclusion to the day's play.

Right then, the first session favored the hosts, with Rachin Ravindra and Daryl Mitchell steadfast at the crease. And will be aiming to extend their lead further as they have seven wickets in hand. The upcoming second session promises riveting action as the contest is getting interesting phase by phase. Stay tuned as the post-Lunch session commences at 6:10 AM IST (12:40 AM GMT).

However, Australia commenced their innings with Josh Hazlewood and Pat Cummins bowling together for the initial half-hour but failed to create any opportunities. Eventually, Pat Cummins successfully dismissed Tom Latham with an excellent review for a caught-behind, terminating the troublesome 44-run partnership. Subsequently, Nathan Lyon and Mitchell Starc were introduced into the attack, but couldn't exert pressure on the opposition batters and conceded runs instead. Mitchell Marsh too, didn't create any chances and inroads as the batters faced the Aussie bowlers with ease. Overall, it was an annoying session for them with the ball. With the new ball just a couple of overs away, Australian bowlers will bat an eye to grab the opportunity in breaking this partnership.

Lunch, Day 3 - Session Summary - 28 Overs, 109 Runs, 1 Wicket. A session unarguably in favor of New Zealand as they managed to extend the lead by 149 runs and lost just a solitary wicket of Latham. As the players head towards Lunch on Day 3, the first session of play has proven to be engaging, to say the least. New Zealand began with Tom Latham and Rachin Ravindra, both adeptly navigating the initial thirty minutes. Tom Latham capitalized on loose deliveries but succumbed to an exceptional delivery by Cummins when he reached 73. Nonetheless, he laid a solid foundation for incoming batters to build upon. Daryl Mitchell, initially cautious, came out with a positive intent and began to accumulate boundaries swiftly, including a six, contributing to the partnership's growth. He initially employed a barrage of reverse sweeps to unsettle the lines and lengths of the bowlers. Rachin Ravindra was watchful as well and the two counterpunched as runs kept flowing in a flurry. Ravindra looked solid in defence and also attacked when he was served poor deliveries. The two together notched up a quick 88-run stand that might surely give them an element of hope.

Commentary.Commentary: The bell has been rung and we are all set to begin Day 3! The players are already out in the middle now. Rachin Ravindra and Tom Latham to resume the batting for New Zealand. Josh Hazlewood to start proceedings with the ball. Let's play...

Now, with Tom Latham still unbeaten on 65 along with Rachin Ravindra on the crease, New Zealand lead by 40 runs. The two will be aiming to yield another strong partnership to extend the lead and take the game out of Australia’s reach. Whereas, Australia, huffed and puffed to create breakthroughs on Day 2 will be banking on their pacers to take quick wickets and ensure the game doesn’t slip far away. This tug-of-war contest is all set to commence in a bit. Stay tuned for the action on Day 3 to begin.

New Zealand sneaked back into the contest first with the ball as Matt Henry shone by taking one of the best bowling figures by any Kiwi bowler, taking a sensational 7-wicket haul and restricting Australia from taking a broad lead. With the bat, despite losing Will Young too early against Mitchell Starc, Tom Latham and Kane Williamson formed a troubling partnership of 105 runs with the veteran knocking a classy half-century. Unfortunately, he couldn’t convert it into a bigger score in his 100th Test match. He was dismissed by Pat Cummins.

On Day 2, Australia resumed their innings with the bat. Marnus Labuschagne and Nathan Lyon constructed a tiring partnership for the Kiwi bowlers but as soon as Lyon went, courtesy of Glenn Phillips taking an absolute screamer at gully, Australia lost quick wickets following some crucial cameos by Mitchell Starc and Pat Cummins. Labuschagne missed his century by ten runs and Australia ended up with a 94-run lead.

Hello and a very warm welcome to our coverage of Day 3 of this enthralling second and the final Test between New Zealand and Australia. The first day belonged to the tourists as they bundled the hosts within two sessions of play. The second day saw a strong resistant comeback from the Kiwis with the bat and taking the lead as well. The third day is not going to be short of thrill and a humdinger contest as this match is moving at a good pace.
...Day 3, Session 1...

Right then, that is it from this eventful Day 2 of this Test. This match has moved at a fast pace and is nicely poised at the moment. New Zealand will be hoping to post a big target while Australia will want to restrict them to as low as possible. Day 3 which could take us nearer to a result will begin on 10th March, Sunday. The first ball will be bowled at 3.30 am IST (10 pm GMT, Previous Day), but you can join us early for all the build-up. Cheers!

Kane Williamson is up for a quick chat. He says that Australia have a quality bowling line-up and says they batted well. He hopes they post a good total on the board on the third day. States there's a bit of bounce and swing and credits Tom Latham for playing a top knock negating the Aussie bowlers. He adds it's a good surface and they have played a number of times on this pitch. Says building partnerships is crucial from here. Further says it's nice to have a lead and ends up saying they have no targets as of now as they are looking to just bat long and implement.

The Kiwis began the third session with authority, as both Tom Latham and Kane Williamson thwarted the Aussie bowlers, capitalizing on loose deliveries and steadily chipping away at the lead. They punished any errant deliveries and gradually surpassed them, with both batters notching up fine fifties and building up a century-run partnership. In a significant milestone, Latham crossed 10,000 international runs. However, Kane Williamson, on his 100th Test, fell just after reaching his half-century to a crucial breakthrough by Pat Cummins. Following his dismissal, the visitors regained momentum, with Cummins and Josh Hazlewood delivering fiery spells. Hazlewood even created a chance to dismiss the set Latham, but Alex Carey's missed opportunity behind the stumps could prove costly for Australia. Despite the scare, Rachin Ravindra and Latham managed to avoid further setbacks until Stumps, ensuring a promising position heading into the next day's play.

During the second session, skipper Pat Cummins showcased a quick-fire cameo, while Mitchell Starc contributed valuable runs, extending their lead to 94 runs before Matt Henry completed his impressive seven-wicket haul. New Zealand aimed to navigate the session without losing wickets, but Starc dismissed Will Young early on, disrupting their plans. Despite Australia's tight bowling, Tom Latham and Kane Williamson displayed resilience, ensuring no further setbacks before Tea.

New Zealand would have been eager to make early breakthroughs on Day 2, and they had a golden opportunity when Daryl Mitchell put down a catch. However, they remained disciplined and battled hard, eventually reaping rewards when Matt Henry dismissed the nightwatchman. Henry continued his impressive spell by removing Mitchell Marsh for a duck, securing a sensational five-wicket haul. Tim Southee's decision to bring Glenn Phillips into the attack proved effective, as he claimed the wicket of Alex Carey. Despite Nathan Lyon's valuable contributions with the bat, Marnus Labuschagne held firm at one end. Just before the Lunch break, Phillips took an outstanding catch to dismiss Marnus, who unfortunately fell 10 short of a well-deserved century.

Stumps, Day 2 - Session Summary - 33 Overs, 91 Runs, 1 Wicket. A remarkable fightback from the Kiwis on Day 2! After getting bowled out cheaply in the first innings, Matt Henry's exceptional seven-wicket haul kept them in the game. Their batters especially Tom Latham and Kane Williamson responded well, but they still need to do a lot more to get ahead in this game. As we go the 'Moving Day', the Kiwis lead by 40 runs. Australia will be a bit disappointed but they still hold the cards in this Test.
A dot to close the day! Outside off on a length, Tom Latham offers no shot at it. New Zealand end Day 2 on a high note with 134/2 on the board. They lead by 40 runs.

SESSION SUMMARY - 78 runs and 3 wickets in 24.4 overs! A hardly-fought session comes to an end! Australia managed to take a lead closer to the 100-run mark with some good hitting from skipper Pat Cummins towards the end. They continued the momentum and Mitchell Starc got them an early breakthrough getting rid of Will Young. They bowled well throughout the session and asked thought questions but just couldn't get any more wickets. The Kiwis bowled the Aussies out inside an hour with Henry ending up with a superb seven-wicket haul. Even though they lost a wicket early, Tom Latham and Kane Williamson looked solid out there and steadied things for them. Both the batters were strong defensively and Williamson also didn't fail to put the loose balls away as they saw out till Tea, reduced the Aussies lead to 51 runs. The hosts will hope that these two extend their partnership further while the visitors will look to make early inroads in the final session and put pressure on the batters. Join us at 8.30 am IST (3 am GMT) to catch all the exciting action in the last session.
